title: Pasta alla Gricia
subtitle: Roman pasta with guanciale and pecorino
excerpt: Gricia is the ancestor of carbonara and amatriciana, but older than either. Guanciale, pecorino, black pepper, and pasta water are all you need. The sauce comes entirely from fat and cheese with no eggs and no tomato.
sourceNotes: Roman pasta alla gricia, widely regarded as the ancestor of carbonara and amatriciana, synthesised from standard Roman pasta traditions.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: This must be made and eaten straight away. The emulsion breaks if it sits.

content.text: The sauce is an emulsion of rendered guanciale fat, starchy pasta water, and pecorino. Get the pasta water starchy by using a smaller pan than usual. Take the pan off the heat before the cheese goes in or it will clump.
Put the guanciale in the cold frying pan. Set over a medium-low heat. Let it render slowly for 10 minutes until the fat runs out and the pieces are crisp. Remove the guanciale with a slotted spoon.
Toast the black pepper in the rendered fat for 30 seconds over a medium heat.
Meanwhile, cook the spaghetti in well-salted boiling water. Save at least 300ml of pasta water before draining the pasta 2 minutes before it is fully cooked.
Add 100ml of pasta water to the guanciale fat. Let it bubble together for 1 minute.
Add the drained pasta. Toss over a medium heat for 2 minutes until the pasta finishes cooking and the sauce starts to cling.
Remove from the heat. Add the pecorino in two additions, tossing briskly and adding pasta water between each. The sauce should be silky and coat the pasta.
Return the guanciale. Serve at once with extra pepper and pecorino.

items.symptom: The cheese has clumped rather than melted.
items.cause: The pan was too hot when the cheese was added.
items.fix: Always add pecorino off the heat and toss quickly with pasta water to loosen.

items.cause: Too much guanciale fat with too little pasta water.
items.fix: Add more pasta water a tablespoon at a time and toss to emulsify.

items.cause: It did not render long enough at low heat.
items.fix: Start in a cold pan and let it render slowly for a full 10 minutes.
